question: Full mental model of how a web page load

answer.text: 1️⃣ Big Picture: What happens when you open a website?
When you type a website URL in the browser, multiple systems work together to locate the server and deliver the page.
Your browser does not magically know where the website is hosted. A chain of infrastructure components resolve and deliver the content.

answer.code: Browser → DNS → CDN → Dispatcher → Web Server → App → Database

answer.text: 2️⃣ DNS (Domain Name System) – The Phonebook of the Internet
DNS converts human-readable domain names into IP addresses.
DNS does not host content. It only resolves domain names to server locations (often a CDN).
A CDN is a global network of servers that cache website content and deliver it from the closest geographical location.

answer.code:
Without CDN:
User in India → Server in US → Slow

With CDN:
User in India → Mumbai edge server → Fast

answer.text: The publisher is the entity responsible for building, deploying, and managing the website.
Dispatcher is a reverse proxy and caching layer placed between the CDN and the application servers.
The web server receives HTTP requests and serves static assets or forwards dynamic requests to application servers.
Static files are served directly, while dynamic requests are forwarded to the application server.
Application servers run the business logic of the system.
Data is fetched from multiple sources.
Caching is easy. Cache invalidation is one of the hardest problems in computer science.
